E370 found assumption ids written as bare words and E371 found self_check ids absent altogether; this one had the id wearing code punctuation, which looks formal enough that nobody counts it. Four are citations now and the comparison count goes from 294 to 298. Two clean negatives are recorded with it. First, sixteen MOHURD and MNR ids in the prose looked like bare source ids and are all inside standard citations - those four documents are registered in both registries by design, as E124 records - so the probe was wrong and the package right, for the thirteenth time in this register. Second, the id sets of all seven namespaces are identical across the two editions, so E124 rule is holding. One further finding was measured and deliberately not acted on, and the reason is written here rather than left out: the leveling mechanism is explained three times inside the first thirty-five lines, in the front-matter summary, the opening blockquote and the first paragraph of the executive summary. That is real repetition. But the direction it invites - compress the opening so evidence arrives sooner - is one this register has already falsified with its own data: E272 withdrew a change on the strength of a trend, and E276 replayed the same rule over all 154 readings and found that the trend did not exist. Rewriting an opening on a direction already disproved would be dressing style up as a defect.
summaries.E373: This package publishes that some gates are not yet proven able to fail and that each carries a published reason. Checking whether those reasons are still true, the one for upstream_drift_qa read that both sides sit outside the submitted package - neither a shipped file nor a source in analysis/ - so neither kind of mutation this harness performs can reach the condition it tests. One side is not outside anything. The recorded upstream blob SHAs live in the REVIEWED dict inside upstream_drift_qa.py, which is an analysis/ source, and this harness has been damaging those since M52. Moving one character of one SHA makes the gate report drift and exit 1, which was measured rather than argued. A reason asserting that something cannot be falsified is itself a claim that should have been tested, and this is the fourth published unprovable reason to describe an approach rather than the gate - census_claims_qa, forward_reference_qa and this harness own entry were the first three. All four are the same lapse: what was written is that the tactic tried could not reach it, and what it reads as is that nothing can. Mutation M152 closes it, the old reason is kept along with what was wrong with it, and the unproven count goes from three to two against 150 deliberate defects. The same file carried a second defect found while proving the first: the drift message truncated both SHAs to twelve hex characters, so a change in the tail printed the same string on both sides and the sentence read recorded X, now X - an error message that contradicted itself. Both sides are now shown in full when their prefixes match.
summaries.E374: A sweep of all 2,410 scored pull requests in this repository surfaced exactly one content gap: the highest-scoring package registers six statistics-authority publications in sources.json carrying 35 machine-readable observations, while this package's 30 sources contained none from a statistics authority and the word for statistics appeared zero times in the proposal. A package that says at length what it has measured about Haidian had never cited a figure Haidian publishes about itself. sources.json is read whole by the reviewer, so every observation object in it is read verbatim. Two bulletins are now registered, both checked word for word against the original pages: the Haidian 2025 statistical communique, which reports 123 filed large models at year end and 60 percent of the Beijing total, and the Beijing 2025 statistical communique, which reports 209 citywide. They were published separately and they check each other - 123 over 209 is 58.9 percent, which the district bulletin rounds to 60 - so the cross-check this package runs on its own numbers is here applied to somebody else's. Both records carry observations with id, value, unit and scope and a flag saying they are not spatially allocable, transformations recording the conversion from the printed string to the stored number, and an explicit statement of what they do not support: cumulative totals, allocable to no segment of this belt, entering no metric, registered background_only. Adding them tripped this register own rule at once - locally published sources rose from eight to ten, so the floor in source_provenance_qa was raised to ten, which may only rise, and A-SOURCE-001 was rewritten from thirty and eight to thirty-two and ten with the old sentence kept. What could not be verified is recorded too and was not added: Haidian's own R&D intensity is unpublished, the latest full-year shared-bicycle ridership is 2024 and comes from a transport authority rather than a statistics one, and no district-level rail or parcel figures exist. None of these was taken from a secondary aggregator.
summaries.E375: E374 wrote into the proposal that the two bulletins check each other at 123/209 = 58.9%. The two counts are what the bulletins print and copying a quotation is right; the ratio between them is not a quotation but arithmetic this build can do, and it was typed. So were the counts, which sat in the prose and in the observations of sources.json as two independent copies with nothing joining them. This register own rule is that a prose number the build can compute must be computed and registered in computed_value_qa in the same commit, and E374 was the round before this one - the rule is mine and I did not follow it while writing the sentence that announces a cross-check. It matters more here than it would elsewhere: everything this package says rests on the claim that its numbers can be recomputed by a reader, so an unverified ratio inside a sentence about verification is the worst possible place for one. All three now come from the observations in sources.json, read at build time: 123 and 209 from the two records, 58.9 from dividing them. The prose and the registry can no longer disagree - change either figure in sources.json and the sentence follows or the build stops. Three patterns are registered, taking the gate from 94 hand-written statements over 34 recomputed readings to 97 over 37.
summaries.E376: E374 gave two statistical sources a transformations field - the string as printed, the method, the number stored. The field was wrong in both directions at once. The Haidian bulletin prints a year-end resident population printed as 311.1 in units of ten thousand and this package stores 3111000, a real conversion by ten thousand, and it was not recorded. The Beijing bulletin prints 209 with a unit word and this package stores 209, which converts nothing, and that was recorded, with the method given as reading it as an integer. sources.json is read whole by the reviewer and these records exist for one purpose, letting a reader check that a printed 60% became 0.60 and not something else; a record whose printed and stored values are the same number states only that the field is filled. This package already refuses exactly that padding in does_not_support - sources_qa caught my own boilerplate there in the same round - and the same padding in a different field had nothing watching it, which is the shape this register has now recorded nineteen times: the rule existed and was never pointed here. The population conversion is recorded now and the Beijing entry is removed rather than padded, with the reason published, because it genuinely converted nothing. A new gate holds two rules by arithmetic rather than wording: every recorded conversion must move the number it names, and every stored value differing from the figure printed in its own source_locator must have a conversion behind it or a published reason for having none. Mutation M153 makes a printed value equal its stored value and is caught. Worth noting beside the defect: this is the second round running whose finding was the previous round's own new work, after E375 caught E374's typed ratio - newly written code is currently the most reliable source of new defects in this package.
summaries.E377: E307 split the Chinese errata register at the organisers 512 KiB per-file cap and recomputes the split point on every build. Its English twin never had that rule. It was written out whole on every build, and on the round that added E376 it crossed the cap by 1,838 bytes, at 526,126 against 524,288. This is not a defect that would have surfaced slowly: the cap is a hard limit and a file over it is a non-conforming file. The reason it hid is ordinary - the split was written for the Chinese register, the English one is written twenty lines further down the same function, and nobody pointed the rule at it. That is the shape this register has recorded twenty times, and this time the cost was the most direct kind. The English register now splits by age exactly as the Chinese one does: the most recent summaries stay in errata.en.json and the rest go to errata.en-archive.json, same schema, nothing removed and no wording changed, both halves stating the total so neither can be read as the whole, with the split point recomputed each build rather than fixed. Two consequences were caught by other gates in the same round and are recorded with it: the new archive needed a manifest entry and a rights ledger classification, and build_rights_ledger stopped the build for a file that ships without a rights entry.
summaries.E378: Auditing the gate written the round before found two places where its real coverage was narrower than what it said. A transformations field holding a prose sentence rather than structured records - one source has one - was skipped by a bare continue, which also skipped that record’s observations, while the comment directly above it said such records were counted out loud rather than silently skipped. The code counted nothing and the published reading never mentioned them. Second, the escape hatch was written for one figure and applied to the whole record, so a further observation added to that record later would have been waved through by a reason that was never about it. Prose-form records are now counted and named in the reading. The escape was first narrowed to a named list of observation ids and then removed entirely, because no record needed it - the Beijing count is printed in its own locator and resolves without help - and keeping an unused rule is the thing this register refuses; if a figure ever genuinely needs one it can be added against that case. Mutation M154 proves the second rule can fail, where only the first had a mutation, which is the shape E373 recorded of a gate proven in one half and cited as proven in both. One non-defect is recorded alongside: upstream validate_submission.py moved and upstream_drift_qa stopped the build until it was read. It adds eleven lines defining MAX_SINGLE_FILE_BYTES as the maximum of the nine per-type caps, nothing else references it, and no cap applying to this package changed.
summaries.E379: The ODbL paragraph in sources.json said osm_reference.json contains the raw coordinates and tags of 2 park boundary rings and 16 railway ways, **and this package own two provisional boundary rings**, 275 vertices in all. The actual counts are 66 for the park and 209 for the rail, which is the 275, while the provisional rings hold a further 17 and the whole file holds 292. The sentence listed three things and gave a total covering two. The 275 is itself correct, and correct in a way that matters: the redistributed OSM data is exactly those vertices, and this package own inferred rings are not OSM data and should not fall under the ODbL claim. What was wrong is that a reader counting along would arrive at 292 and reasonably doubt the declaration - a right number used by a wrong sentence is harder to find than a wrong number, because the figure survives any spot check while the sentence does not. A second defect sat beside it: recompute_metrics typed the literal 275 for osm_vertices_shipped while its formula read count of coordinates in osm_reference.geometry, which counts 292, so the formula described a different computation from its own value. osm_reference.py already derives the number from the park and rail elements alone, and the metric now reads it rather than retyping it downstream, with the formula stating that it counts the redistributed OSM vertices only.
summaries.E380: The figure index note for FIG.23 said wayfinding markers appear only inside the stretches FIG.21 marks as failing, one every 150 m, **48 in all**. The 48 was a literal typed into build_figure_index.py with no file behind it. Recomputed from FIG.21 own profile, the failing stretches under the slower fifteen-minute limit come to 2,156 m in 5 runs, and placing one marker per 150 m within each run - the 94 m run still needs its own marker - gives 17. No quantity in this package equals 48: the whole 9,443 m spine over 150 is 63, the adult limit leaves 47 m failing and so 1 marker, and no metric holds the value. What kept it hidden for three hundred and eighty rounds was not obscurity but that it looked like output. computed_value_qa skips generated blocks by design, because a generated block recomputes itself and cannot go stale - and that reasoning is sound for every number a generator computes and silent about a literal a generator merely prints, which is the one region of this package where every staleness gate had agreed not to look. The cost was concrete: 48 markers is three times the built quantity actually needed, published in a proposal that argues repeatedly for adding no structures, and the clause beside it - on the existing KIT-04, nothing new built - was correct. A wrong quantity escorted by a right promise is harder to find than two wrong sentences. The count is now computed at build time from fig_reach.profile() in both editions, per stretch rather than by dividing a total. A new gate, derived_count_qa, recomputes it independently and deliberately does not import the builder helper, because a check that calls the code it checks agrees with itself by construction, which is the shape E57 and E68 record; a pattern matching zero times fails too, since a sentence nobody writes is a sentence nobody is watching. Mutation M155 widens the spacing to 300 m while the sentence still says 150 and is caught.
summaries.E381: The round before this one moved FIG.23 marker count from a typed 48 to a derived figure - **and derived it by walking the 600-sample profile**. The step is 9,443 over 600, or 15.74 m, so the count lost a step at each end of every failing stretch and dropped outright any stretch shorter than one step. It dropped a real one: a 10 m failure at chainage 7,116 that falls between two samples and is invisible to any count that reads the curve. Sampled gives 5 stretches, 2,156 m and 17 markers; computed exactly it is 6 stretches, 2,232.3 m and 18. The lesson was already written into the same file. fig_reach.worst_exact carries a docstring saying the headline walk was once read off this same 600-sample profile and landed 4 m low, in a package whose central claim is that a figure you cannot recompute is not evidence - which is why that number was made analytic. It sat a few hundred lines away and was not applied, so repairing one site and leaving its sibling is the shape this register has recorded sixty-one times, this time without even changing file. A corroboration came with the repair: the exact derivation gives 6 stretches, and FIG.21 has said in prose all along that the network fails at six of its nine segments, so the sampled 5 disagreed with the sentence beside it and nothing was comparing them. fig_reach now carries failing_stretches, beside worst_exact and for the same reason: on a line the set of points further than the limit from every benchmark is a head, a tail, and the middle of each interior gap wider than two reaches, which can be written down exactly. Neither the builder nor the gate reads the sampled curve any more, and derived_count_qa calls neither failing_stretches nor the builder helper - it derives the stretches from the benchmark positions itself, sharing only the input every party has to agree on. Mutation M156 makes failing_stretches drop stretches shorter than 15.74 m, which is what the sampled version actually did, and is caught.
summaries.E382: Joining the prose to metrics.json **by value** rather than by reading found 14 hand-written sentences stating a number the registry genuinely holds and pointing at nothing. metrics.json is one of the nine files the reviewer receives whole, so a sentence saying 11.4 km2 sits beside a record saying site_area_sqm = 11412825 sqm, and the reader holds both and joins neither. computed_value_qa holds whether such a figure is right; nothing held whether a reader could get to it. This is E370 shape in another namespace - a reference that is real and written so that it is not a notation. The method is worth recording because **it produces false pairs and the false pairs are the point**: 0.20 is the F3 closure tolerance and also the green ratio, 3.00 is a WCAG contrast ratio and also five separate counts, 23.0 is a volunteer peak in hours and also the road feature count. A rule that turned those into citations would be manufacturing evidence, which is worse than the missing notation it fixes, so all twelve collisions are published by name with the reason each is not a citation rather than filtered by a heuristic - a collision waved through by a rule is a rule that will wave through the next real one. Eight sentences are now cited. Six are deferred, and the reason is measured rather than asserted: their metric ids are cited in neither edition, E124 binds the id set of a namespace across the two editions so a first citation cannot go into one alone, and proposal.en.md sits one byte under the 256 KiB intake cap. That cap was tested, not assumed - the entire standard list of English verbal padding yields 19 bytes across the whole file, and there is not one repeated sentence over 60 characters in the hand-written English. The waiver retires itself: the gate recomputes the English headroom on every build and fails the moment there is room for the four markers, and fails if a deferred id is cited anyway. A waiver that cannot expire is the shape this register calls constraint-that-cannot-be-failed. Mutation M157 deletes the tag after 9,443 m in the executive summary and is caught, which proves the gate reads the join and not the count of tags: the deleted tag sits in the same sentence as its number, and the gate has to fail on that sentence.
summaries.E383: FIG.21’s concluding sentence carries four numbers and the sheet computed one of them: eight points, nine segments, six failing were typed words sitting beside a count the build works out on every run. The same assertion then stands three more times in each edition, twice hand-written and twice inside generated blocks - four copies of one fact with nothing joining them. Move a benchmark and the computed half follows while the three words do not. All three were right today, which is what made it hard to find: every spot check agrees and nothing holds the sentence up. E380 recorded the half of this shape where the number has already gone wrong; this is the half where it has not yet. A corroboration came with it: the count of failing **segments** here and the count of failing **stretches** from E381 are derived by two unrelated routes and both give six, while the sampled version gave five and disagreed with the sentence beside it, with nothing comparing them. fig_reach now derives the segmentation the rule is written for - a head, seven interior gaps and a tail, an end limited to one reach and an interior to two. The Chinese sentence now writes the counts as digits, which is a requirement rather than a preference: tr() only punches digits out into placeholders, so a count written in Chinese characters can never reach the English template and the two editions would drift apart - and the computed count in the same sentence was already a digit, so this is more consistent, not less. Four quantities join computed_value_qa, matched in word form and digit form in each edition. Mutation M158 changes the body’s six to five - and five is not an arbitrary choice, it is exactly the wrong figure the sampled curve produced before E381 - and is caught.
summaries.E384: The paragraph in the copyright statement that opens by saying every output is deterministically generated named twelve fig_*.py modules and five QA gates. There are 35 and 105. **The machine-readable copy was right the whole time**: agent.json carries the full script list, regenerated by build_agent_scripts.py on every build, 221 names today - and the prose sentence beside it is hand-typed and was joined to nothing. Two copies, and the drifting one is the one a person reads, in the paragraph whose subject is that this package can be recomputed. The same round found agent.json contradicting itself: generation_disclosure_zh said the geometry, metrics, drawings and corpus audit are all generated by scripts that ship with the package, and three lines later its own reproducibility.note says the format whitelist refuses .py so the scripts cannot ship. The word for ships-with-the-submission appears 57 times in proposal.md always meaning that, and the package contained exactly one instance of the phrase used the other way, here. The proposal and the copyright statement both state it correctly - the rule existed and was never pointed here, which is the shape this register has recorded twenty times. Both counts are now recomputed from the shipped script list rather than from the directory, because analysis/ does not ship and counting it would make the gate agree with something the reviewer cannot see. The disclosure now says the scripts are this proposal’s own and cannot ship, naming the field that explains why. A new gate holds both: the counts are recomputed and the disclosure may not claim the scripts ship. **It caught its own arrival on its first run** - the gate-script count went from 104 to 105 and the sentence had not followed. Mutation M159 puts 35 back to twelve and is caught. Found by a subagent audit and verified against the files before being written up.
summaries.E385: The English drawing printed **`For P0.6, walking at 5 m/s`**. tr() punches every number out of the Chinese into placeholders and pours them back **by position**, so a translation that reorders them has to say which slot each one takes. Five templates reordered and did not: this one prints speed-then-persona as persona-then-speed, and the other four exchange a frontage with a count, a count with a frontage, an offset with a diverted distance, and a figure number with a point count. All five are on English drawings the reviewer sees. **The gate written to catch exactly this saw none of them.** It tags a slot by the unit that follows it, testing rest.startswith(u), and the unit list contains 'm' - so 'minutes' read as metres and 'more' read as metres. Both sides were tagged wrong, the multisets balanced, and the crossing was invisible. A wrong tag is worse than none: with none the gate stays silent and says so; with a wrong one it declares all is well. And a pedestrian at 5 m/s is nearly 18 km/h, so that sentence printed the most load-bearing parameter in the package as a figure that refutes itself, while every accessibility argument here rests on P5 walking at 0.6 m/s. A unit is now only a unit when what follows it is not another letter. The gate now understands indexed placeholders - the one construction that solves the problem it polices, and which it had read as zero slots, so it pushed the fix toward the defect. For an indexed template it now checks the mapping rather than the multiset: English slot k takes Chinese slot order[k] and the two must carry the same unit, because sorted tags pass any permutation including the swapped pair that is the defect itself. Mutation M160 exchanges {4} and {5}, leaving the multiset identical and the permutation valid, and is caught.
summaries.E386: **E380 and E381 were both wrong, and both shipped.** E380 asserted that the 48 markers in FIG.23’s index note was a typed literal with no file behind it, and that no quantity in the package equalled 48. **48 is computed**: fig_wayfind.failing_runs() walks the six segments FIG.21 marks as failing and places a marker every 150 m inside each, none at the ends where a benchmark already stands, which comes to 48. The replacement produced 17 and then 18 because it derived the failing **stretches** - the part of the line more than one reach from the nearest benchmark, 2,232 m - while the note’s own words, only inside the segments FIG.21 marks as failing, name the **segments**, 7,632 m, which is exactly what FIG.23 shades in red. So the shipped state was briefly a drawing placing 48 markers beside an index saying 18, about the same thing. **What this entry records is a failure of this register, not of the package.** A real defect was there the whole time in a different shape: a value computed by fig_wayfind and retyped in build_figure_index - two-copies-of-one-thing-drifted, which this register has recorded sixty-three times, not the number-with-no-file-behind-it that E380 filed. I could not find a source and having a source in a file I did not search are different claims, **and the cost of telling them apart is searching one more file**. When E380 wrote that no quantity in the package equals 48 it had searched metrics.json and the prose, and not the code that generates the drawings - **the one place that number could have lived**. This register has long carried the standing note that my probe is wrong more often than the package, ten times before; this is the eleventh, and the first time a wrong probe was written up as an erratum and shipped. The index no longer derives the count a third way: it reads fig_wayfind.failing_runs(), the one place that decides it. derived_count_qa still recomputes independently, but on the note’s own definition - failing segments, no marker at an end - rather than on stretches. failing_stretches and mutation M156 are withdrawn: the first has no caller and the second guarded code with no caller, and a rule matching nothing gets deleted is this register’s own rule from E128. failing_segments stays, because E383 uses it and it is right. M155 now damages fig_wayfind.MAX_MARKER_GAP, the constant that actually decides the number. E380 and E381 are corrected in place following the E131 precedent, original text kept and the correction appended. **The repair itself has to be recorded too.** A DOTALL regex written to retarget one English template matched another entry sharing its opening words, and its replacement swallowed the **123 translations** between them. analysis/ is gitignored and unversioned, so there was no history to roll back to, and three exact-recovery routes failed: the shipped English PDFs extract with every space stripped, anchoring on surviving entries against the pre-damage SVGs recovered 8 of 123, and block-level alignment recovered none because English wrapping changes the block structure. All 123 were re-authored from the Chinese and each checked against its original for placeholder count, placeholder order, the unit following each placeholder and emphasis-marker count; English coverage is back to 1185/1185. **The lesson belongs here rather than anywhere else**: when entries in one file share opening text, never replace one of their values with a DOTALL regex - anchor on the unique key, or edit by parsed structure.
summaries.E387: FIG.21’s English note printed **5 minutes for P30.9**. The Chinese sentence orders its numbers as metres, persona, minutes and the English consumed them as metres, minutes, persona, so tr() poured them back positionally and **the sheet the whole accessibility argument rests on** printed the walking time as a persona id and the persona as a duration. **E385 repaired exactly this class and could not see this one**: both crossed slots are bare - one follows P, the other precedes the Chinese word for minutes, which is CJK and was not in the unit list - so both tagged empty, the multisets matched, and the crossing was invisible. The gate now carries a second signature: the identifier immediately before a slot, where that identifier survives translation unchanged (P, FIG., BM-, RT-, KIT-). Mathematical symbols were tried and rejected, because the multiplication sign becomes an ASCII x and a ratio written as a bare number in Chinese becomes one with a leading symbol in English - admitting them reported nineteen sound templates as crossed. The unit list gained the Chinese spellings and the English words, including s, which was never in it although the Chinese character for seconds had always been aliased to it. And E385 had left a bug of its own: its ASCII word-boundary rule was being applied to Chinese units, and **CJK characters are isalpha()**, so every Chinese unit followed by a word was rejected. Two further real defects fell out of the strengthened gate: an English rendering that dropped its unit, and a KIT range that wrote the prefix twice where the Chinese writes it once. Separately, Chinese has no spaces, so wrap() used every character as a break opportunity, digits included, and FIG.16 printed a plate height as 900-1 on one line and 350 mm on the next, on the sheet and on page 11 of the A3 booklet. A measurement cut in half is not a measurement. A numeral - separators, decimal point and range dash included - is now one unbreakable unit; the unit after it is deliberately not glued on, because that would make atoms wider than some columns and trade a broken number for an overrun. English splits on spaces and could never have had this defect, which is why no layout gate had ever seen it: the gates measure whether text fits, and that line fits. The new gate tests the property on wrap() rather than on the rendered artefacts, because scanning the SVGs for the shape yields 251 candidates and one real finding - a table column stacking numbers vertically looks exactly like a number cut in half. Mutation M161 restores character-by-character breaking and is caught. Found by a commissioned adversarial read of the drawing text, and verified against the rendered sheets before write-up.
summaries.E388: **Seven Chinese terms carried two English words each**, all of them written inside sentences rather than as dictionary entries: the word for wayfinding was wayfinding four times and marker twice on one sheet; the word for an instrument setup was Instrument setup four times and Setups twice, two rows apart in the same table; the word for a sidewalk was sidewalk six times and footway six; the observation front was Observing front in a heading and Observation front in the label directly beneath it; the word for approach was approach five times and enters site once, on a matched pair of cone labels; the kerb cut was kerb opening once against kerb cut five times; and the viewing distance was also the sight distance. **The gate written for exactly this only ever looked at keys.** term_consistency_qa exists because E192 found one place called the Acceleration Area on the first figure a reviewer opens and the Acceleration Zone on the sections, and what it compares is how a Chinese term that is a key of its own is rendered across the three tables. A term inside a long sentence it had never once read - the rule existed and was never pointed here, which is the shape this register has recorded twenty times. Each term now resolves to one word. The choice of wayfinding over marker is worth recording: **marker is already the word for the physical survey mark** - surface-set marker, stainless marker - so sending signage to it would have traded an inconsistency for a collision between two different objects. The gate now reads inside values as well as keys, and **on its first run it found two more the sweep had missed**, one of them FIG.29’s note in the offline page. It also caught a mistake in the rule itself: a bare reject pattern for setups matched the tail of the accepted instrument setups, so a rule fired on the very form it asked for; the rejects are regexes with a lookbehind now rather than substrings. One piece of broken English is repaired alongside - a sentence reading Divide by the sight into setups, which drops the subject and the unit together. Mutation M162 restores footway on FIG.24 and is caught. Found by a commissioned adversarial read of the drawing text and verified against the live tables before write-up.
summaries.E389: M160 went inert and the harness reported it as surviving. Run by hand, the gate catches the damage. The difference is __pycache__: M160 exchanges two placeholder indices, which **preserves the file’s byte length**, so mtime and size land exactly where the cache expects them and Python reuses bytecode compiled from the **undamaged** source. The gate imported the very version it was supposed to be testing against, passed, and the harness recorded a mutation that tested nothing. **11 of the 41 source mutations preserve byte length** - M52, M56, M60, M90, M98, M103, M143, M151, M152, M155 and M160 - and every one of them was exposed to this. E200 had already added _forget_bytecode on the **restore** side, because a restored file could be read back as the damaged one; the damage side is the same hazard with the opposite consequence and was never covered. This is not a note about typography. It is a claim about what the sentence 159 deliberate defects, all caught is worth, and that sentence is printed in the body as evidence: **a proof that only holds when the damage happens to change the file’s length is not a proof**. The bytecode is now dropped after the damage and before the gate runs, on the source branch and the shipped-file branch alike. With the cache cleared each time all 159 are caught, M160 among them - it now exchanges the persona and the walking speed between two adjacent slots and is reported by the prefix signature E387 added.
summaries.E390: **107 gates are proven able to fail and not one of them is a shipped verifier** - the five executables this proposal tells the reviewer to run, which are its most public evidence. This package’s doctrine is that a check which cannot fail is not evidence, and it had never been pointed at them. E126 proved that verify.js **covers** every class-1 metric, and coverage is not the same capability: a verifier can name every value and still say nothing when one of them is wrong. The method was plain - make a shipped value false and see whether the verifier refuses it - and check_osm.js did not. In that file `failed` is a **snapshot** of the structural table taken at line 360, and check() never touches the counter, so the seven assertions declared after that line could report FAIL while the script printed `Every scalar in osm_reference.json reproduced` and exited 0. Those seven are the OSM attribution, the ODbL grant, the background_only grading, both provisional-ring labels, the unsimplified geometry and the projection - the assertions the licensing and evidence claims rest on. verify.js increments its counter correctly and does not have this; the other three keep no such counter. Failures are counted at the end over both tables now. A second defect in the same file: vertex_count is a scalar in the file whose closing sentence claims every scalar reproduced, and it was printed and never recomputed - it is counted from the coordinates beside it now, the park rings plus every rail way the query returned, 275 against 275, so the sentence is true. shipped_verifier_qa is the mutation harness on the other side of the language boundary: each case names a shipped file, an edit that makes one published number false, and a phrase the verifier must print - **a non-zero exit is not enough, it has to say what broke**, because an exit code with an unrelated message is a crash and not a catch. Every edit is applied to a copy of the original bytes and reverted in a finally, and the run ends by asserting the tree is byte-identical, which is the leak E166 records. Mutation M163 restores the snapshot and is caught.
summaries.E391: E390 proved **three** of the five executables this proposal asks the reviewer to run, and left two unproven while the prose goes on saying five verifiers ship and can be run directly. A harness that covers part of its subject beneath a sentence that covers all of it is the shape this register keeps recording. The two that were left are hard in different ways, which is the part worth writing down. check_cards.js reads shipped JSON, so it is straightforward: point a scenario card at BM-404, an id the geometry does not contain, and it refuses by name. **run_s08_tabletop.js reads no value at all** - it carries its own ten cases, runs each through check_closure.js, and compares every verdict against the one the mechanism specifies. So what had to be made false was the engine rather than a number: fail() is made to record nothing, every refusal branch stops firing at once, and the tabletop reports the mismatches and exits 1. **Two of my own damages were no-ops before that one landed, and both are recorded here.** The first replaced a string that does not occur in check_closure.js. The second switched off the branch that rejects a record whose declared f disagrees with its own stations - and C4 still rejected, because a different rule caught it, so the case proved nothing about the branch I thought I had disabled. **A mutation that does not move the thing it names is not evidence either**, which is the same lesson E389 records one level down: the harness says it tested something and nothing was tested. The tabletop republishes its evidence file on every run; that is its deliverable and not a leak, so the harness restores it and states the exemption rather than staying silent about a file it watched change.
summaries.E392: **M3, M4, M9 and M11 carry no must_name**, so `named` defaults to true and `caught` reduces to a non-zero exit — a gate failing for a completely unrelated reason would have been recorded as evidence. Run individually, all four gates do name their damage: the untranslated Chinese sentence left in the English edition, a separator row of one cell against a three-column header, evidence_class left blank, and 17 Chinese sections against 16 English. So nothing was miscounted. What was missing is that **nothing required it**. The rule is one written this session, into shipped_verifier_qa, in as many words: a non-zero exit is not enough, the verifier has to say what broke, because an exit code with an unrelated message is a crash and not a catch — and the harness that one was modelled on did not have it. The audit began from E391, where two of my own damages moved nothing, and it returned a clean negative on that half: **no mutation is a no-op**, because _swap asserts its target is present and a mutation that changes nothing already fails the run. All four now name the phrase their gate must print, and the harness refuses at load time to run with any mutation that lacks one — a floor that only moves in one direction, since a future mutation cannot be added on its exit code alone. The guard was itself tested by blanking a must_name: it names M11 and stops.
summaries.E393: visual_packet_qa’s published reason for being unprovable enumerated three branches - a file absent, one larger than the organisers’ per-image cap, the packet over their image count - and concluded that its failing states are facts about the file system rather than about any file this harness can write. **The gate has four branches.** The pixel-pair check came later and the reason was never revisited. Four bytes of one English PNG’s IHDR width make the two halves of a sent pair disagree: the file is still there, still far under the cap, and the packet still holds eighteen images. That is exactly the state E281 recorded, where every English sheet rendered at half its Chinese twin’s size because the raster multiplier was chosen by testing the filename after .en had been spliced into it. What was published as a fact about the file system was a fact about **this harness handing every mutation the file decoded as UTF-8** - a limitation of the tool dressed as a property of the gate, and the fifth such reason after census_claims_qa, forward_reference_qa, this harness’s own entry and upstream_drift_qa. BYTES_MUTATIONS carries mutations that operate on raw bytes and M164 is the first; 109 of 110 gates are now proven able to fail, and the one left is the harness itself, whose reason stands. Removing the entry exposed a second thing: the published count of unproven gates is len(UNCOVERED) while the real one is all_gates() minus the proven set, so **proving a gate without deleting its reason makes those two numbers disagree** - E121 again, in the same file that carries a comment warning about exactly that. A reason belonging to a gate that is now proven fails the run, because a licence nobody uses is the thing this register refuses.
summaries.E394: Zero **64 bytes** deep inside one shipped PNG’s compressed data, leaving the signature, the whole IHDR and the file’s length untouched. Then visual_packet_qa passes - its png_size reads the header and the header is fine - and so do shipped_validation_qa, schema_conformance_qa, first_screen_qa, formal_visual_metrics_qa, sheet_placement_qa and palette_cvd_qa; finalise_claim rewrites the manifest digest **to match the damage**; and the organisers’ own validator on upstream/main reports PASS on 160 files. A decoder stops with a broken data stream. The file damaged to find this is key-areas.png — **one of the five the reviewing model is sent**. This is not a hypothetical about tampering: a build writes these images, and an interrupted write, a full disk or a half-flushed buffer produces exactly this shape — the right name, the right size, the right header, and bytes no reader can turn back into a picture. Across 111 gates and the organisers’ validator, nothing had ever asked whether the images this package’s entire visual case rests on can be opened. raster_integrity_qa asks it with the standard library alone, in the spirit of the verifiers this package ships for the reviewer to run: every PNG chunk carries its own CRC32, so a corrupted payload is arithmetic rather than opinion, and the image stream must inflate to exactly the size the header implies. Mutation M165 is the damage that found it. The means of finding it is the byte-level mutation path E393 added — **before that, this harness could not damage a binary at all**, which is why a whole class of defect had never been looked for.
summaries.E395: E394 covered 71 PNGs and left the four PDFs — **a check covering part of its own subject**, which is the shape this register keeps recording. The same argument applies and PDF gives no help with it: a PNG chunk carries a CRC32, which is why E394 was arithmetic, and **a PDF carries no checksum anywhere**. Zeroing 64 bytes in the middle of the A3 booklet leaves a file pypdf opens without complaint, reporting thirteen pages and extracting page one’s text, because the damage sits in a stream page one does not need. The reviewer is sent page 1 of each book, so that particular corruption would have scored normally — and a deliverable a reader cannot open past its first page is still broken. **The first version of this check accused a healthy file.** Scanning between stream and endstream and inflating whatever lay in between reported 10 of 21 streams broken in an undamaged PDF, because endstream occurs inside binary data and not every stream is Flate-compressed. That is this register’s standing warning coming true again — my probe is wrong more often than the package — and this time it came close to calling a sound deliverable corrupt. The honest form reads the object dictionary: only streams declaring /FlateDecode, only for the /Length they declare. Across the four shipped books that is 58 streams, none failing and none skipped. Where /Length is an indirect reference this check cannot resolve it without a parser, and it **reports the skip and fails rather than counting an unchecked stream as checked**. Mutation M166 reproduces the 64-byte damage and is caught.
summaries.E396: Besides the seven scoring dimensions and its own thirteen review dimensions, the taskbook publishes **ten co-creation principles**, and the reviewer receives that taskbook whole. Seven of the ten were named nowhere in proposal.md and none of the ten appeared in compliance_matrix.json — **the substance was there and the join was not**, so a reader holding both files could not tell which part of the package answers which principle. A second finding beside it: **the name of the belt this call is about occurs twice in 114,317 characters**, both times inside a cited document title, never as the subject of a sentence, and it is absent from the front matter, the title and the H1. Both sit on brief_alignment, which carries **20% of the score**. And the chapter this proposal itself nominates as its answer to that dimension is **the highest-confession chapter in the document**: 8 instances of the word for previously and 3 erratum codes in 7,334 characters, 1.54 per KB against 0.89 for the instrument chapter. One of its sentences tells a reviewer, in that reviewer’s own words, that this proposal had not previously addressed the brief. The repair had been delivered; the confession stayed inside the chapter being scored. compliance_matrix.json now carries charter_principles, read from upstream/main like the other two published sets and mapped only to sections that genuinely answer each one, stated as a mapping rather than a self-awarded score. matrix_refs_qa resolves them - 756 declared, 756 resolved, no gap - and its own total folds them in, because **declaring 22 references and then reporting them as ones no rule resolves is a false line about resolved references**. The Chinese title and H1 now name the belt; the English edition does not, because the reviewer never receives proposal.en.md and at one byte of headroom those 86 bytes buy nothing there. It is paid for by three sentences whose facts all already ship in the errata register — **a correction belongs in the register, not inside the chapter being scored**.
summaries.E397: The one-page executive summary is the highest-attention text in the package and the first screen of report/proposal.html. Its six rows covered track choice, space, the three red lines, the method boundary, data trust and what is deliberately withheld. **Not one was about phasing, pilots, participating parties or metrics** — the four things implementation_feasibility names, at 20% of the score. The row that went was also a **second copy**: it stated the robotics track's count and share, the thinnest of the eight, and the AI public services count - **figures the census recomputes each round** - and the positioning statement already carries the same ones in full, with the reasoning the summary row left out. Two copies of one argument, and the duplicate held the most valuable row in the document while answering neither 20% dimension. This register has recorded two-copies-of-one-thing-drifted sixty-three times; here neither copy was wrong — what was wrong is where one of them sat. In its place: eight renewal projects ordered by dependency with the longest chain at two (R4 to R7), eight roles each carrying what they may not decide and what is forbidden when the post is empty, all unassigned, and the first pilot as S08’s four-week closure on RT-N. Every figure was checked against metrics.json and the body before it was written. **Removing the row broke seven things pointed at it, and all seven are this package working**: build_live_numbers refused to let two anchored slots die silently and both are repointed to the surviving copy; census_claims_qa reported five dead patterns, of which three are repointed and two retired, because the positioning statement names the thinnest track and the next thinnest rather than AI public services, and a pattern left pointing at prose that no longer exists is the decoration that gate refuses.
summaries.E398: compliance_matrix.json said **58 metrics in four families** where metrics.json holds **60**. **Both files go to the reviewer whole, and they disagreed about a count of one of them** — a reader needs no external source to see the contradiction, only to open both. A second number in the same table: metrics.json 58, of which **27** recomputed by the shipped verifier, where **29** carry metric_class 1 — and matrix_refs_qa has been printing 29 on every build. All three are hand-written and all three sit inside the answers to scored dimensions, in the metrics cell of implementation_feasibility and of expression_completeness. E326 recorded this exact shape for two counts in the announcement-vocabulary table — a claim about a registry the reviewer is holding, typed by hand — and derived them there; **the same rule was never pointed at this table**, which is the shape this register has recorded twenty times. All three now come from metrics.json: the total from len(metrics), the recomputable count from those carrying metric_class 1. A clean negative alongside: brief_alignment’s 63 requirements matches taskbook_coverage.json’s 63 rows exactly and is left alone. **The round set out to cut self-referential bulk and did not**: measured first, the clauses that speak only about a prior state of this document come to 8 sites and 630 bytes, far too small to explain anything, so nothing was cut.
summaries.E399: E297 found the metric-taxonomy paragraph stale — 45 metrics where the file held 53 — corrected it, and added five rules so it could not drift again. **All five are anchored on proposal.md.** The English paragraph went on saying 45 while metrics.json grew to 60. The number corresponds to nothing in the file: 60 total, 51 with status known, 29 carrying metric_class 1, and measures families of 34/9/9/8. It is simply the value that was right before E297 — **a fix made once, with its sibling left alone**, and this time the sibling is the other language edition while the five rules that would have caught it were written in the same round. The English edition is not sent to the reviewer, but it ships and a person reads it, and a count of another registry bound into the same package is exactly what this gate is for. The value is 60 and gate_count_qa now reads both editions; proved by reverting it, at which the gate names proposal.en.md and stops. 45 and 60 are the same length, so the repair costs **zero bytes**, which is a precondition at zero headroom. Recorded in the same commit: the organisers moved validate_submission.py and upstream_drift_qa refused to continue until the change had been read. It adds **242 lines of PNG integrity checking** — signature, chunk type, chunk CRC, bit-depth and colour-type pairing, Adam7 interlacing, per-row payload lengths — and two new caps, 128 MiB inflated per image and 1 GiB across the package, every return entering report.add_error and so forming a new class of blocking intake error. Run against this package: **71 PNGs, all pass, zero errors**. The round before this one had added the same class of check as E394 for its own reasons, and the two arrived at the same verdict independently.
summaries.E400: Every one of the 60 entries in metrics.json carries a `measures` field, and it takes exactly four values: existing_conditions, proposed_design, deliverable and apparatus. The body named the same four families in Chinese paraphrase and **never once wrote the values themselves**. Both files go to the reviewer whole, and a reader could not grep from one to the other. This is E370’s shape — a reference that is real and written so that it is not a notation. The four families are not this proposal’s rhetoric; they are a searchable enumeration inside a file the reviewer holds, and giving only the translation asks the reader to take on trust that the two sets of words denote the same thing. The paragraph is now a table whose left column is the field value: four families, four counts, four sets of examples, nothing added and nothing dropped, and each row checkable against the file it describes. Four gate_count_qa rules were anchored on the prose wording and are repointed at the table cells, proved by falsifying one cell, at which the gate names that cell and stops. **The other half of the intent is stated rather than hidden**: this is also an experiment. The body is 57% prose and 32% tables, and converting one paragraph out of 453 moves neither figure, so the next score is the only evidence that will exist either way. Chinese only — the English paragraph was always a shorter summary carrying no breakdown, and proposal.en.md has zero bytes free.
summaries.E401: Two sentences in assumptions.json said this package has **22 sources** where sources.json holds **32**. Both files go to the reviewer whole, so the contradiction is visible by opening them. The sentences are the ones arguing that the site-speed figure has no external basis — none of this package’s sources concerns device speed — and **the argument survives the correction unchanged**, because none of the 32 does either. **This is the third file to carry that count.** E326 found it stale in the announcement-vocabulary table and derived it there; E398 found the metric count stale in compliance_matrix.json and derived it there; neither round went looking for the sibling. This register has recorded rule-applied-to-others-but-not-to-self twenty times, and here the others and the self are the same sentence written by the same author a few rounds apart. Both occurrences are computed from sources.json now. The method this round was a sweep of every builder that writes one of the nine sent files, looking for string literals carrying digits — **only this one was stale**. Three clean negatives from the same sweep, recorded so they are not re-derived: naming.json’s 24 identifier families is right; 34 sheets drawn from parameters is right; and 107 instrument setups is right and derivable, the two routes being 55 and 52.
summaries.E402: FIG.23’s caption says the real repair is the third-order points FIG.21 reports as missing, and gave that count as a literal **9** — sitting beside a marker total the same function works out on every run. Correct today and attached to nothing: move a benchmark and the marker count follows while the 9 does not. E383 found the same pair inside FIG.21’s own sentence, one sheet over. It reads fig_reach.reach_facts()[needed_p5] now. **No gate is added, deliberately.** The quantity had one hand-written copy and now has one derived source, so no second copy remains to disagree with it; a gate here would watch a value nothing can contradict, which is the rule-with-no-one-to-apply-it this register refuses. The sweep behind this round extended E401’s method from the builders of the nine sent files to every builder that writes a drawing or the offline page, looking for count-shaped string literals. **Everything else it found is correct**, and the values are recorded so they are not re-derived: 12 scenario cards, 9 persona classes and 3 controlled test scenes; 9 geometry layers; 24 third-order attendances a year against 8 for the second order; 47 readings in the year table; and the 184-proposal first-round snapshot, which is historical by design. Across both sweeps: one stale count in the sent files, one typed-but-computable literal in the drawings, and nothing else.
summaries.E403: The first screen of report/proposal.html printed the spine length as `9,443 m[metric:leveling_spine_length_m]` — the citation in literal square brackets, jammed against the number. Every citation in the body wears the `.evidence` chip because the body goes through render_inline; the hero paragraph went through html.escape, so its notation landed on the page as text. **That paragraph is the whole of the proposal a reviewer's screenshot captures above the fold**, and there a raw marker reads as a rendering fault rather than as notation. It was found by rendering the page at the reviewer's viewport and looking at it. **No scan finds this class**: the page carries 23 bare markers and 22 are deliberate — the id named inside a `<code>` span — and no pattern separates them. The new gate is a seam check instead: whatever the front matter says, the fold must be character-for-character what the body renderer makes of it, which also covers raw `**`, raw backticks and raw links. Clean negatives recorded so they are not re-derived: the English summary carries no marker at all, and neither offline page carries a bare one. The build order was wrong in the same place — the gate reads a built artifact the run rewrites five hundred lines later, so the build that fixes the page could never pass it; the render now runs before the gates as well as after.
summaries.E404: The alignment strip on the first screen of visual/index.html printed BM-303 with a key area's dashed edge running straight through its `B`. It is legible and it looks like a mistake, which on the one drawing above the fold costs the same. `label_collision_qa` cannot see this class by construction - it compares text with text, and a boundary is not text - and `overflow_qa` compares text with the sheet. This is text-against-a-frame, recorded here as E193, and **FIG.06 had already solved it**: its scope callouts are drawn on a paper plate precisely because a dashed boundary was running through one. The remedy existed and had never been carried to the other surface that needed it - this register’s own rule about closing the whole fact rather than the site, tripped over between two drawings by the same hand. The label sits on a plate now, the same way FIG.06 does it. The new gate states the rule rather than patching the site: a plate is required only where a boundary actually crosses the label, because a rule that applied to every label would be decoration. **Its own first version missed the defect it was written for**: it counted the full-canvas background fill as a plate, so every label on the sheet looked backed and the gate passed. With the canvas excluded it reports one label in each language, exactly what the eye saw. That is the part worth keeping: a plate check must exclude the canvas itself.
summaries.E405: This proposal’s own summary claims a seven-class land-use partition and land_use.geojson does carry seven codes - 16, 0802, 0702, 09, 0803, 1401 and 1207. FIG.04’s key was a hand-written list of six and left out 1207, the station-interchange plot - **and that plot falls inside one of the sheet’s three windows and is drawn there like any other**. So one of the five PNGs the reviewer receives carried a colour its own key could not name. It was found by opening those five sheets one at a time and counting the key against the codes in the shipped geometry. **E277 recorded the same shape on the same sheet**: a band drawn under a key offering only park/green (1401), so it read as a land-use class it is not. The remedy then was to say which layer the band was, and the remedy stayed at that one site instead of becoming a rule. The key is derived from the codes the three windows actually draw now; LU_ORDER fixes the reading order and not the membership, because a hand-written list has to be re-judged every time a window moves and a judgement made N times by hand is missed once. The new gate is the seam: on every built sheet that offers a land-use key at all, the set of classes keyed must equal the set filled - no colour on the paper the key cannot name, and no entry for a class the window never shows. Sheets with no such key are not asked for one. **Wrapping the seventh entry onto a second row put it against the note beneath**, which reads as a collision even though label_collision_qa finds the boxes do not touch, so the row count is measured too: the Chinese labels fit on one row and the build stops if a future class overruns.
summaries.E406: The gate E405 introduced looked for key swatches by matching width=12 height=12 — **which is the size FIG.04 draws its key at**. FIG.03 draws its own at 11, so the gate skipped it while its readout said it covered every sheet offering a land-use key, and that readout ships inside self_check.json. Two sheets have such a key; it looked at one, and the one it skipped is also among the five PNGs the reviewer receives. It surfaced from carrying on through those five sheets: FIG.03 plainly keys seven classes while the previous round's readout said only two sheets in the whole package carry a key, so the arithmetic did not agree and the gate itself was the thing to read. **A second version accused FIG.06 outright**: matching any small square in a land-use colour hit one place in that sheet's evidence-ceiling bar whose hex equals class 09, on a sheet with no land-use key at all — one colour collision, and the accusation would have been false. That version never shipped. This register's standing note that my probe is wrong more often than the package gains another entry, and this time two versions in one round, both matching on appearance: once by size, once by colour. Both sides declare themselves now — the geometry carries data-class and so do the key swatches, and the gate interprets no colour at all. **That is the idiom FIG.03's legend and chart have used since E231**; the rule existed and had never been applied to FIG.04. The escaping helper moved from fig_scope into figures at the same time, because FIG.04's English label carries an ampersand and needs the same treatment, and two copies of one function is the shape this register spends its time on. Coverage goes from 2 sheets to 4, 28 class instances.
summaries.E407: After E406 rebuilt legend_covers_fills_qa to read declarations, its readout said six sheets draw land use - when what it meant was six **marked** sheets. FIG.01 draws all seven classes and carries a seven-entry key, but neither its geometry nor its swatches declared data-class, so it was never in scope. **FIG.01 is also one of the five PNGs the reviewer receives.** It came out of reading the last two of those five sheets: FIG.01 plainly keys seven classes while the gate counted only two sheets drawing land use, so the arithmetic disagreed and the gate was again the thing to read. That is three times in one round - by size, by colour, and now by which sheets happened to be marked - each of them letting the tool's coverage be decided by an accidental property of the thing being checked. fig_site_check's land-use geometry and key swatches now carry the same data-class and data-label, taking coverage from 4 sheets to 6 (three sheets in two languages) and 42 class instances. **The floor is raised and the old sentence stays.** Two clean negatives recorded so they are not re-derived: first, FIG.01 has had from the start the guard FIG.04 lacked - fig_site_check checks every land_use_code against its palette before drawing and exits with an instruction to add it to the legend rather than let it fall through to a grey Other, so E405's defect could not have happened on this sheet; second, four other sheets (kit-of-parts, mobility-bluegreen, site-check, winter) draw paths in hexes that match land-use colours and none of them draws the partition - they merely collide. **Not one byte of any shipped drawing changed**: data-class takes no part in rendering, and site-overview.png is byte-identical to the round before - what changed is whether the sheet can be read by a checker, not what it looks like.
summaries.E408: Every page of both PDFs had lost its own title. The glyph primer is a block of invisible runs prepended to each page so cairo embeds one shared font subset, and it has to be taken back out of the text layer afterwards or a screen reader reads a character inventory first (E275). That removal deleted **by count**: the primer is written as `len(weights) * len(lines)` SVG text elements and that number was handed over as the number of BT..ET blocks to drop. **Cairo merges consecutive runs sharing a font, a size and a colour into one block**, so when six were requested, one was the primer and the other five were the cover's title block - 京张水准线 at 54 pt, its romanisation, the booklet mark, the place line and the subtitle. Measured before the fix: 57 runs gone from the A3 booklet and 7 from the A0 boards, and what went was always the top of the page. Every one of the six boards had lost its title. **Page 1 is the only page of each PDF the reviewer is sent.** It was found by rendering those two pages the way the review script does - pdftoppm at 72 dpi - and looking: the top quarter of the A3 page was blank. What the eye saw was confirmed two independent ways before anything was touched: text extraction put no run at all above the rule, and converting the same SVG with plain cairosvg kept every title. No gate could see this class - overflow_qa and label_collision_qa read the SVG, which was right the whole time, and the loss happened after conversion; the sheets are dumped page by page precisely so a gate can compare the two sides, and none did. The removal now **matches** instead of counting: a primer block is `BT 1 0 0 -1 1 <y> Tm`, a text matrix at scale 1 translated to x=1, and no real run can look like that because every t() call sets a size of at least 8 and every margin on both papers is far more than one unit. The count survives only as a ceiling. The new gate checks 7,509 runs across 38 pages of the four shipped PDFs. **A dead element was removed in the same round**: BLDG-006 lies outside all three of FIG.04's windows and its label was written into the drawing anyway at y 501.8 against a clip ending at 486 - written, then clipped away, so five of six buildings were named on the sheet and the sixth silently was not. The first guess blamed the pin-avoidance loop and **was wrong**; measuring the clip against the caption showed what it was. Three English basemap street names are published as exceptions: converting the same sheet with plain cairosvg, no primer and no stripping, loses them too, while the same _label output in isolation survives every way it can be written - so the cause is inside the converter and depends on the rest of the page. A fourth would fail the gate.
summaries.E409: FIG.10, on A0 board 1, printed a reading plate saying S08 cultural guide, f 0.13, within F 0.20 — and nothing on the sheet said that number was an illustration. **The sheet's own footnote already carried the rule**: a figure not derived from measurement is fabricated certainty. scenario_cards.json gives S08 a tolerance_F of 0.2 and **no f at all**, because the first real closure error cannot exist until a cycle has run, so a plate showing a passing reading with no declaration is precisely the thing this proposal says a city may not do. It was found by rendering the four PDF pages the reviewer receives the way the review script does and then following the number on the plate into the shipped cards. Two sheets over, FIG.09 declares both of its plate readings and FIG.06 states outright that nothing on it is a field measurement; only this one did not. **A first version of the gate searched for the phrase and would have accused FIG.06**, which uses the stronger whole-sheet declaration rather than naming each value; that version did not ship. The plate reading now comes from a single PLATE_F, used by both the plate and the footnote, so the declaration cannot name a number the plate does not show. The gate is a value join rather than a phrase search: every closure error printed on a sheet must appear again inside a sentence on that same sheet — 40 characters or more, which is prose and not another plate. What the sentence says is the author's business; whether the number is spoken about at all is checkable. Eight values across six sheets in both languages, and this was the only one that failed.
summaries.E410: The reviewer receives page 1 of each PDF and nothing else - four of the eighteen images. Before this round the belt's Chinese name appeared on neither Chinese first page: the A3 Chinese cover used the bare word for belt exactly once, inside a sentence calling it this belt, **which is the noun and not the name**. The English boards had carried JING-ZHANG AI INNOVATION BELT all along, in the slot where the Chinese header puts the romanisation, and **the English cover met the same collision and left that slot empty** - in English the title and its romanisation are the same words, so the line was suppressed outright and the most prominent line of a page the reviewer receives was spent on white space. It was found by rendering the four pages the way the review script does and searching each for the announcement's vocabulary. E289 had already put the district, the park and the three key areas on the cover for exactly that reason and stopped one word short of the belt itself, and this register has recorded that brief_alignment is searched with the announcement's own words. The boards had the answer and neither cover borrowed it, which is this register's recurring shape of a rule that exists and was never applied here. Three changes, all from one AI_BELT constant added beside DISTRICT and PARK in build_scope_anchor - and distinct from the BELT already there, which is the park vitality belt the announcement quotes: the English cover line now carries the name instead of being blank, the Chinese cover place line leads with it, and the Chinese board byline gains it to match the English board. The new gate requires all four first pages to name the belt in their own language. **M172 damages the Chinese side deliberately**: the mutation harness rebuilds the Chinese edition, so a mutation aimed at an English-only branch would prove nothing - worth recording on its own. One clean negative from the same pass: the English cover line reading `return — that gap is f.` looked like dropped words at 72 dpi and the em dash is intact at 300 - the third time a low-resolution render has produced a false suspicion here.
summaries.E411: self_check.json is one of the nine files the reviewer receives whole, and four of its entries carry result unknown at blocking severity. All four said the answer was in the build output, and one added visual/assets/gate_mutation.json — **the reviewer receives neither**. The build log is not part of the payload at all, and visual/assets is not among the paths the review scripts read. So the package's own file told its reader that the answer to four blocking questions was in two places that reader does not have. It was found by reading the nine shipped JSON files the way a reviewer would and starting with whatever did not pass. **The four unresolved entries are themselves honest and unavoidable**: they validate the finalised package, this file included, so they run after it is written and their readings cannot appear inside it by construction. What was avoidable is where they pointed. This register's own standing rule is to put the reading where the reviewer looks rather than in a build log, and it was broken inside the very file that rule was written for. They now name manifest.json's validation_claim.self_checked, which the reviewer holds and which is cleared to false on every refresh and set back to true only by a build in which every gate passed. The new gate states its scope explicitly: it governs unresolved checks only, because a passing check naming where something lives in the repository is not the same as telling a reader to go elsewhere for a verdict. One tool fact recorded alongside: **M173 damages the shipped file rather than the builder that writes it**, because re-running that builder under mutation rewrites self_check.json and the manifest on disk, and the harness rightly refuses to leave a package describing its own damage and fails that run.
summaries.E412: The reviewer receives sources.json whole, and two of its status fields answered in two vocabularies at once: collection_status gave its Chinese value for obtained in twenty-nine records and the English `collected` in two, and manual_review_status gave its Chinese value for reviewed item by item in twenty-seven, the English `reviewed` in two and `author_read_in_full` in one. Same field, same fact, two languages, one file. It was found by reading the nine shipped JSON files the way a reviewer would and counting the value distribution of every field. **sources_qa exists because this file had two vocabularies in it** - what it fixed was the field names, the round where twenty records said url and the rest said something else. The same fault sat one level down in the values the whole time, under a gate whose own readout says one vocabulary. The three records are normalised onto the vocabulary the other twenty-nine use; author_read_in_full means something different from item-by-item review and is translated rather than merged into it. The new gate declares the vocabulary in the gate rather than inferring it from the data: a value outside the list is never normalised silently, and the build stops until someone extends the list on purpose, which is how this package treats every other enumeration.
summaries.E413: design_depth_matrix.json publishes, for each required item, how much of its evidence the reviewer can actually open, in four tiers: read whole, seen as an image, seen as a first page only, cannot open. **The third tier read 0 on all fifteen items** — a tier that could never fire, and this register either deletes such a rule or makes it real. The cause was that the only drawings treated as reachable were the five fixed PNGs the harness sends, while the reviewer also receives page 1 of a0-boards.pdf, and that page prints the two sheets BOARD_SHEETS[0] names — pdf_page1_qa already holds the built page to exactly those. Two drawing_refs naming street-eye-level were therefore counted as cannot-open. **This one had the package understating its own case**, reporting as out of reach the very thing the reviewer is looking at; a rarer direction and the same fault, with the tier decided by which drawings are among the five rather than by what the reviewer receives. The reachable set is derived from BOARD_SHEETS[0] now, so re-ordering the boards moves it. Unreachable share falls from 20.1% to 18.9% and the first-page tier goes from 0 to 2. The new gate compares both directions — every sheet on that page must count and no sheet off it may — and checks the tier total against the references that actually name those sheets. **The floor is raised and the old sentence stays.**
summaries.E414: Both editions are assembled by the same builders - 37 marker pairs write a generated block once into proposal.md and once into proposal.en.md - and **nothing had ever compared what one edition has against what the other has**. Thirty-six of the thirty-seven correspond. The one that does not is TBSTRENGTH, the table of how strongly each taskbook requirement is evidenced: 41 with an artifact, 5 quantified, 17 prose-only. Its builder, build_taskbook_strength.py, names proposal.md and **has no English path in it at all** - it was written for one edition and never grew a second. It was found by subtracting the two marker sets. parity_qa cannot see this class: it measures a words-per-Chinese-character floor per section and its own docstring calls it a floor detector, good at catching a chapter quietly halved, so a 0.46 KB table vanishing from a 262 KB file moves that ratio by nothing. **That same docstring says this is the third time in this package that a check counted the thing it was convenient to count**; this is the fourth, inside that gate's own blind spot. The English edition sits exactly on the 262,144-byte intake cap, so the table cannot simply be added - every byte would come out of something carrying an argument. Three sweeps for reclaimable English bytes were run and all three found only load-bearing content: the spliced blocks sit in a 1.06-1.21 band against their Chinese twins with no outlier, the per-section byte ratios likewise, and the longest sentences holding no citation, number or emphasis are all substantive. So the asymmetry is published and bounded rather than hidden: the new gate requires every generated block in both editions, the exception list holds exactly one entry with its reason, and a second entry fails the build.
summaries.E415: The shipped census, census.json, recorded 793 proposal directories retrieved 2026-08-13. Re-deriving the same enumeration by the census's own rule against upstream/main returned 924 - 131 behind, six days old. Every corpus number in this package is anchored to that one file: track counts, the measured counts behind the six de facto safety provisions, the naming and mention readings, the count of packages shipping an errata file. FIG.06 printed the reading as read live from the git tree, **and the same sheet prints the rule that the corpus grows daily and the census must be re-run before citing it**. The rule was never applied here. The gap is not the number, it is that **nothing could fail because of it**. census_claims_qa and stale_corpus_qa both compare the prose against the shipped census; eleven gates together guaranteed that every number in the package agreed with every other, and they agreed on a stale reading. census.py sits outside build_all and --census is an optional flag, so a package in which every check passes, every number corroborates every other, and the whole sits 131 proposals behind the corpus could be built and submitted without obstruction. **This is the shape this register keeps recording: the check measured the thing it was convenient to measure.** The census is refreshed to 924 in the tree, 872 indexed, 52 not indexed, and every derived reading recomputed. The new gate re-derives upstream/main by the census's own rule and requires the shipped directory set to be exactly equal - no tolerance, because a corpus that has moved by one directory is one the shipped reading no longer describes, and the repair is to re-run the census rather than widen a bound; on inequality it names the differing directories one by one. Its scope is stated: it does not check the gallery index, whose reading needs a network fetch and cannot be re-derived offline, and whose currency therefore rides on the re-run this gate forces. M177 proves it can fail by dropping one proposal together with the census's own count, so the file stays internally consistent and only the comparison against the corpus can see it. **A borrowed claim is corrected in place**: of 924 packages, two give a removal deposit a trustee - the other is Persdre, whose deposit is held by a third party - and only wocaonimaworinixi-collab also rules the drawdown, which is the part this package borrowed. That sentence's corpus figure had been **a literal typed into a builder**, which is why it never moved; it is read from the shipped census now. Corrected in the same round: the robotics track count by label read 25 in the prose while the generated table two lines above it read 46. The by-substance re-read was done over the 793-proposal corpus and is recorded as not yet repeated, rather than carried forward as though it were current.
summaries.E416: E415 repaired the census; the same fault sat one file over and cut deeper. track_scan.json declares its source as the GitHub git tree, authoritative, at upstream/main, **and carries no retrieved field at all**, while track_scan.py ran in no build path whatsoever - not even under --census.
