The deeper layer: that script writes only analysis/track_scan.json, which is gitignored, so **the shipped copy was placed by hand and had no link to the script that produces it** - re-running the scan changed nothing the reviewer receives. The scan therefore rested at 40 proposals while the two tracks it scans reached 129, and all eleven probe counts and shares in that file were divided by 40 and quoted item by item in the prose. The whole argument that this proposal's increment lies where the field is silent rests on that one denominator. ship_census_data() had existed here all along and was simply never extended to this file: **the rule existed and was never applied here.** It surfaced by taking E415's measure straight to the sibling files, which is the value of a fix - treating it as a class rather than a site. track_scan.py joins CENSUS_STEPS, track_scan.json joins ship_census_data(), and census_currency_qa gains a second stage: the scan's population must equal the number of proposals declaring either track in the shipped census, with no tolerance. M178 proves it can fail by shrinking the population together with its own roster, so the file stays self-consistent and only the comparison against the corpus sees it. **The match rosters named authors only**, and the 129 packages come from 120 authors - five ship two packages each, so three probe rosters carried a repeated name that could not be checked entry by entry; they now read author/package, each pointing at exactly one. Three edition drifts nobody had caught are corrected in the same round: the charging-mention count read 27 in Chinese and 26 in English, and the appeal time-limit count excluding this proposal read 5 in Chinese and 4 in English; 27 and 5 were right. The sentence saying only 3 proposals touch siting, 2 other than this and naming both, no longer holds - it is 16, and the roster goes back to the shipped file rather than into the sentence. After this fix: a denominator of 129, with appeal time limit 16, bond or insurance 40, jurisdictional seams 4, emergency access 10, charging or parking 88, and charging siting 16.
summaries.E417: E415 and E416 were the same defect twice, and both were invisible for the same reason: **the file could not be placed in time.** The census carried a retrieved field and was caught the moment anyone looked; track_scan.json carried no date, declared itself authoritative, and sat at a denominator of 40 against 129 for weeks. Following that thread: eleven shipped assets name an origin outside this package and **seven of them carried no reading date at all**. The worst was review_gate_survey.json, which calls itself GitHub GraphQL, every pull request in open-city-ai/haidian, not a sample - a totality claim - while reading a cached snapshot of 1069 pull requests against a repository that held 3438. The script defaults to report mode, which reads the cache; fetching needs an explicit argument. With no date, the totality claim reads as present tense. **A mistake made in this round and recorded here**: the first stamp wrote the date of the run, which would have marked a 1069-PR cache as read today - worse than carrying no date at all. The date has to follow the data, not the run that reads it. fetch() now writes its date into the cache and report() carries it through, and an old undated cache makes the script exit with an error rather than invent one. The re-fetch took it from 1069 to 3438 pull requests, so the totality claim holds again, and all four would-flip conclusions still read zero on 3.2 times the sample. manifest_schema_survey went from 855 manifests to 926, its failures from 75 to 74; spatial_level_survey from 371 submissions to 925 and from 20 shipped spatial.json to 70. The same pass found that **osm_stitching.py also wrote only to analysis/**, and its hand-placed shipped copy had decayed into a strict subset, missing the arterials and arterial_segments_in_site fields entirely, with nothing connecting the two sides; it joins ship_census_data(). The new gate derives its scope from the shipped files rather than listing them by hand: any asset whose own source or method names upstream/main, GitHub, GraphQL, OpenStreetMap or Overpass must carry an ISO retrieved date, with four exemptions each carrying its reason - three regenerated from the package on every build, so dated by manifest.generated_at, and census_history, a historical series with a date per row. Its scope is stated: it checks that a reading can say when it was taken, not that it is current, which is census_currency_qa's and is exact there. After this fix: 11 externally sourced assets, 7 carrying an ISO reading date and 4 declared exempt with the reason.
summaries.E418: FIG.22 publishes two walking speeds in so many words - 0.6 m/s for persona P5 and 1.2 m/s for a general adult - and says the benchmark-spacing rule follows P5 rather than the adult figure. Meanwhile reach_check.py fixed its ten-minute reach limit at a typed 800 m under a comment calling that ten minutes at 1.33 m/s, **the walking speed this package uses elsewhere**. It is used nowhere else. Ten minutes at the declared 1.2 m/s is 720 m. build_whitespace_rules.py carried a harder claim still: 800 m as **the organisers walk standard** - and searching brief/, scripts/ and schema/ at upstream/main returns no walking distance published by the organisers at all, the only circle named in the brief being a fifteen-minute one. The number 800 m is not itself wrong: the national residential standard and the brief both associate it with fifteen minutes. What was wrong was the minute count pinned beside it, and calling it the organisers standard. A distance typed beside a speed drifts from it; a distance computed from it cannot - and this distance is the threshold in rule W1, which a reader applies to decide whether a block passes, so moving it without moving the rule changes the ruler and leaves the graduations alone. reach_check now holds ADULT_WALK_MPS and WALK_MINUTES and computes the limit; build_whitespace_rules reads it rather than keeping a second copy, and the W1 text states the conversion. **The corrected readings run against this proposal**: buildings within a ten-minute walk fall from 232 to 183 today and from 261 to 206 once linked, the gain from 29 to 23, and the served area from 203.3/220.6 ha to 164.1/178.4 ha. The new gate requires the limit to equal the declared speed times the declared minutes, requires FIG.22 to still publish both speeds, and requires the prose to state the distance; its scope says it does not judge whether 1.2 m/s is the right adult speed, which is a design judgement published for refutation, and does not govern P5 0.6 m/s. M180 proves it can fail. In the same round the 232/261 pair moved from typed to derived and entered computed_value_qa - **they had been in no watch at all**, so the limit could move and leave them behind. After this fix: 720 m, and 183 / 206 / 23.
summaries.E419: E418 concluded that a distance must be computed from a speed rather than typed beside it. Held to its own measure, **that fix typed its own copy of 1.2**: reach_check.py declared ADULT_WALK_MPS while the authoritative value sits in the shipped personas.json, whose own note reads that changing these numbers changes four sheets together - which a typed copy defeats. The same pass found **P5 speed of 0.6 m/s typed into six modules**, and worse, that figures.py **already had** walk_speeds(), reading all three speeds from personas.json, with a docstring saying four sheets had each held their own copy and that they agreed today while nothing would say so tomorrow. The mechanism had been there all along and these places had never used it. **A mistake of mine is recorded here**: the first fix added P5_WALK_MPS and ADULT_WALK_MPS constants to figures.py, which is a second source of truth - the very thing being removed - and was reverted once walk_speeds() was found. A checker holding its own copy of the value it checks proves only that two typed numbers agree, so the gate now reads personas.json too. reach_check reads the declared adult speed, leaving 720 m unchanged but making that sentence in personas.json true of this limit as well; fig_reach and fig_evidence use walk_speeds(). walk_speed_qa grows a third stage: the limit equals the declared speed times the declared minutes, FIG.22 still publishes both speeds, and **five drawing modules may not hold a copy**. That stage has to be exact: fig_routes draws a rectangle at 0.6 times the scale and fig_steplink a band at 0.6 times the pixels-per-metre, and neither is a speed - the first version matched bare literals and reported both falsely, so it now matches only the two shapes that can only be a speed. M181 proves the new stage can fail. After this fix: one declaration for each speed, read by five drawing modules and one computation.
summaries.E420: Each of the three scope levels publishes a re-survey cycle beside a column naming the benchmark orders that level contains. The orders have their own cycle table - the one FIG.04 and FIG.09 draw, and the one the cost model is built on: origin and first annual, second quarterly, third monthly. **The published 47 sessions a year is exactly that**: 1 origin and 2 first at annual, 2 second at quarterly, 3 third at monthly. Nothing in it pays for a half-yearly or quarterly first-order run. Yet the scope column read annual, half-yearly, quarterly, and the two rows marked half-yearly and quarterly name the first-order routes and BM-0 with the two first-order points. **The three copies had already drifted before this fix**: proposal.md read annual, half-yearly, **annual** while FIG.03 drew annual, half-yearly, **quarterly** - the same row, and **both are surfaces the reviewer receives**, the body whole and FIG.03 as one of the five sent images, with nothing ever comparing them. A neat ladder parallel to the three scopes is not a derived fact. The cycle is now derived from the orders each level names, taking the coarsest because that run is what closes it, held once in build_reading_calendar and read by fig_scope, build_visual and the body table. **[Corrected in-register, see E422] The sentence that stood here was wrong.** The first derivation converted every level at the cadence of its *points*, which turned the overall design scope from a correct half-yearly into annual - that row names the *routes*, the spine and the two connecting runs, and the FIG.09 signage table publishes RT-N / RT-S connecting routes at a half-yearly whole-route re-survey beside first-order *points* at annual. **Only the key-area row was actually wrong**: it names the datum and the two first-order points, the body read annual and FIG.03 drew quarterly, and annual is right. The new gate requires every published cell on all three surfaces to equal the derived value; its scope says it does not judge the order cycles themselves, which the cost model rests on, nor the per-point calendar, which reading_calendar_qa holds. M182 proves it can fail. After this fix: all three levels annual, derived from the orders they contain.
summaries.E421: printed_difference_qa guards one subtraction: the body prints 11,472 m and 9,443 m, and their difference must be written as the 2,029 a reader gets by subtracting the two printed figures, not the 2,028 that comes from subtracting the underlying values and rounding. But its test was **wrong in text - any occurrence of those digits anywhere in the whole document**. It fired this round on a sentence three chapters away reading that there are 9 files, 1337 KB and 2,028 entries to read: a count, in a sentence printing neither operand. It fired today only because build_review_route grew from 2,011 entries to 2,028. **This is the same shape as two other repairs the same day**: a gate being heuristic where it has to be exact. The first version of the E419 stage searched for bare numeric literals and falsely accused a rectangle drawn at 0.6 times the scale; this one searched for a bare difference and falsely accused an entry count. A check that can collide at random with a forbidden number as the corpus grows will eventually point at a correct sentence and call it wrong - and the first standing note in this register is that my probe is wrong more often than the package is. The test now narrows to the single unit that carries both operands, split by sentence and table row: 2,028 is only a claimed difference where it stands beside 11,472 and 9,443. After this fix: 6 surfaces print both readings, 4 of them state the difference, and every one states it as 2,029.
summaries.E422: **E420 changed a correct row into a wrong one.** The FIG.09 signage table publishes two lines side by side: BM-1 / BM-2, first-order *benchmarks*, annual re-survey; and RT-N / RT-S, the *connecting routes*, a half-yearly whole-route re-survey. A first-order route and a first-order point do not share a cadence. E420 derived every scope level at the cadence of its points, so it turned the overall design scope from a correct half-yearly into annual - and that row names the first-order survey lines, the spine and the two connecting runs, which are routes. **Only the key-area row was actually wrong**: it names the datum and the two first-order points, the body read annual and FIG.03 drew quarterly, and annual is right. E420 caught that one and broke another on the way past: one derivation, applied to the wrong kind of object. No gate caught it, because the gate E420 added only confirms that three surfaces agree with the derivation, and the derivation itself was wrong. **What caught it was opening the A0 board the reviewer actually receives and reading it.** The derivation now branches on whether a level names routes or points; the route cadence lived **only inside fig_kit.py**, a second lone copy, and moves into build_reading_calendar with the signage table reading it back. E420 is corrected in-register in both editions with the old sentence kept, and M182 is retargeted to the row that was actually wrong. After this fix: annual, half-yearly, annual.
summaries.E423: The A3 booklet cover carries a paragraph on the ground within a ten-minute walk of a benchmark: 183 buildings today, 206 once linked, a net 23, and a served area moving from 164.1 to 178.4 hectares - **all of which had already been recomputed at the 720 m limit E418 derived** - while the last sentence of the same paragraph still read **800 m of network distance, not a radius**. Two quantities contradicting each other inside one paragraph, **printed on one of the four page-1s the reviewer is sent**. E418 did not reach it because **walk_speed_qa scoped itself to proposal.md**: it held the 720 m in the body and could not see the drawings. A gate holds the surface it is pointed at and no other. The same pass found that the English template in i18n_drawings.py writes the distance as a parameter, so the English cover had already followed the derived limit while the Chinese had not - the two editions had drifted on that sentence with nothing comparing them. All three typed copies of 800 now read WALK_LIMIT_M: the cover sentence the reviewer receives, the assumptions note in reach_check, and the English line in its docstring. The gate widens to every dumped page in both editions and names the page when a superseded distance is printed beside the words for network distance. M183 proves it can fail by typing the cover sentence back the way E418 left it. After this fix: cover and body both 720 m, all three derived from WALK_LIMIT_M.
summaries.E424: sources.json reaches the reviewing model whole, and its `observations` are the only machine-readable **external** measurements this package publishes. Of the four, the Haidian bulletin's resident population - printed as 311.1 in units of ten thousand, stored as 3111000, its conversion duly recorded - **appears in no sentence of either edition**. It sits in the same list as three numbers that do carry the argument and reads exactly as they do. Every other registry here is closed against its own use: source_citation_qa requires every registered source be reached from the body in both editions, the depth matrix requires the same of each of its items, and metric_citation_qa joins the published metrics to the prose by value. **`observations` was the only registry with no reachability check**, and it is the most evidence-like column in the file. More exactly: inside this same record the package had already refused to write a read-as-an-integer conversion for the Beijing bulletin, on the stated ground that such a record says only that the field is filled - **and that same ground had never been pointed at the column beside it**. All four observations now carry a boolean `cited_in_argument`; the uncited one also carries `not_cited_reason_zh/en` saying it was read and not used, and why it is published rather than deleted: keeping only the figures that were used would leave no way to tell a page read whole from a page read selectively. The new gate observation_reach_qa checks both directions. Marked cited, and both editions must carry a line holding this record's own [source:] tag beside a printed form of the number, so the figure is reached through the record that published it rather than merely present somewhere. Marked uncited, and the reason must be given in both languages and neither edition may cite it, so the flag cannot go stale once the number is later used. M184 and M185 prove each direction can fail. After this fix: 4 observations, 3 reached through their own [source:] tag in both editions, 1 declared unused with a stated reason.
summaries.E425: FIG.06 is one of the five PNGs the reviewing model is sent and metrics.json reaches it whole, so the sheet's roll-call of a metric class and the register itself are two copies of one fact inside the reviewed set. **Class 2 had drifted in both directions at once**: it named the road redline, which is not a metric but a component that setback_m already declares it covers, and it omitted existing_residential_floor_area_sqm, which is a class-2 metric carrying a full published reason. **The completeness rule already existed and covered one of the three classes**: CLASS1_ORDER is compared against the register on every build, so class 1 cannot lose a member, while the class-2 and class-3 lines printed directly beneath it were typed strings that nothing compared. Class 3 happened to be correct, which is exactly what made the panel read as uniformly derived. The heading was too narrow as well - awaiting official controls describes four of the five members, while the residential floor area waits on ownership and survey data rather than a regulatory plan. Both lines are now derived from metrics.json by metric_class in both editions, the heading widened, and figure_metric_class_qa holds set equality both ways: a metric the register places in the class and the sheet does not name fails, and a name the register does not hold fails. M186 and M187 prove each direction. **The first attempt repeated the same defect it was fixing**: it put the rule in the renderer as well as the gate, so damaging the label map killed the render before the gate could run and neither mutation proved anything. The renderer no longer enforces - a member with no label is simply not printed, which is the drift the gate names. After this fix: 5 class-2 and 4 class-3 metrics, every one derived from the register and named on the sheet.
summaries.E426: The three key areas are the announcement's own proper nouns. compliance_matrix.json and proposal.md both reach the reviewing model whole, and **each named one area three different ways**, while site-overview.png - one of the five images it is sent - printed a fourth: 45 non-canonical mentions across 7 shipped files, typed independently by fourteen build scripts. **The first attempt at this fix was wrong and the build refused it twice, correctly both times.** The rule began as make everything match the organisers' geometry. But compliance_matrix.json's label_zh is copied verbatim out of their agent_taskbook.json, so rewriting it would have made this package misquote the taskbook inside a file the review reads whole; and taskbook_units_qa requires the heading answering a taskbook unit to carry the taskbook's label, or a reviewer searching the taskbook's words cannot find the section. Read side by side from upstream/main, their taskbook writes one transposition and their geometry the other, and **both are theirs** - while neither file ever puts a space around AI. **So the drift that was actually ours is the spacing, not the transposition.** The rule narrowed to: every mention must equal, character for character, a string some organiser file publishes. That forbids the spacing variants we invented and lets each official form sit where it belongs - the taskbook's spelling where a section is named, the geometry's where a geometry feature is, and the organisers' own wherever a field of theirs is quoted. Twenty-five sites across eight scripts, seventeen in compliance_matrix.json, three section headings, and two in English where one place was both Acceleration Area and Acceleration Zone - the defect E192 recorded and fixed only in the translation tables. **No gate was added**: the Chinese side became a third layer inside term_consistency_qa, whose own docstring already said two Chinese keys differ only by the spaces around AI - that rule had simply never been pointed at the shipped Chinese. After this fix: 77 mentions of the three areas, every one character-identical to a string an organiser file publishes, and no spacing variant of our own.
summaries.E427: proposal.en.md reaches the reviewing model whole, and one Chinese name for the connecting route carried two English renderings inside it: **closing route(s) six times, connecting route(s) six times**. **One of the two is wrong, and wrong in the most expensive place.** A fuhe levelling line runs from one known benchmark to **another** known benchmark; the loop that returns to its start is bihe - and this package's central term is **closure error**. Rendering fuhe as closing collapses it into the same root as bihe, and the difference between them is what makes the mechanism mean anything. This package's own E16 states it: a connecting route is checkable because it ends on a second independently known point. **E174 already caught this exact pair and fixed it only where it was looking.** That erratum records six places where one Chinese name carried two independent English translations, closing routes against connecting routes among them — but it compared figure titles against captions, and fixed the figures. The term kept both wordings in the body prose, where six survived. term_consistency_qa should own this class, yet it compares the keys of three translation tables, and this term's English is typed directly in builders and prose and never passes through a table: **the rule existed and was pointed at another surface.** Standardised on connecting route across thirty sites in eleven build scripts including both translation tables, four hand-written sentences in proposal.en.md, and one hand-maintained field description in closure-record.schema.json. **Fixing it, I damaged the register and record that too**: a sweep across analysis/ also replaced the pair E174 quotes **as evidence**, turning it into connecting routes against connecting routes — a sentence claiming to record two independent translations, with the same word on both sides. Restored one by one. **A sentence that quotes a defect must still read as that defect after the defect is fixed**, which is the same rule this package follows for the organisers' fields and for other people's corpus text: quotations are not normalised. After this fix: the connecting-route term has one English rendering, connecting route, across both editions, every sheet and the schema, and the sentence in E174 quoting the two old renderings stands word for word.
summaries.E428: proposal.en.md reaches the reviewing model whole. The Chinese term for the reading plate appears ten times in the Chinese edition, and the English edition gave it **two names**: reading plate five times, reading board three. **This is the third occurrence of the class E174 named and E427 fixed one instance of.** term_consistency_qa compares the **keys** of three translation tables, while this term's English is typed partly into build scripts and partly into prose and never passes through a table: **the rule exists and is pointed at another surface.** Which rendering wins is not a preference: KIT-02 is the component's formal name and it is the reading plate, and in the same sentence the benchmark inscription is already rendered plaque - the Chinese character for a sign maps to plate and plaque throughout this package, and board was the single exception. Standardised on reading plate across four entries in i18n_en, two in build_scenario_cards, one in fig_street, and three hand-written sentences in proposal.en.md. Plate and board are both five letters, so **the English edition is byte-identical** at 262,112. **One site was checked and deliberately not changed**: an i18n_en entry rendering a wrapped caption looks as though it drops the inscription, and does not - the caption breaks across four keys in Chinese, the inscription falls in the preceding segment as plaque, and all five standard parts survive the wrap. **The finding came from a method worth keeping**: rank English bigrams that share a head word and differ only in the tail, both occurring at least three times. One pass produced this erratum and a clean negative beside it - third-order point against third-order benchmark, where the Chinese itself carries a long and a short form and the English mirrors them one for one. Most rows are genuinely distinct concepts, so the table is to be read rather than applied. After this fix: the reading-plate term has one English rendering across both editions, every sheet and the translation tables.
summaries.E429: Page 1 of a3-booklet.pdf is one of the four PDF images the reviewing model receives. The cover printed the value of oversized_built_count under the label **non-park oversized blocks** (English: Oversized blocks, not parks), but the shipped formula counts cells over 4 ha whose park, campus, water and heritage shares are **all four** below 50 percent - **the label named one of the four exclusions**. The body prose named two. **Read through that label the number describes a much larger set**: excluding only parks would sweep in the campus, water and heritage superblocks, which are exactly the ones this package argues should not be treated as fabric awaiting repair. The definition lives in one boolean in build_fabric; the label was a hand-written phrase at four sites, and **a judgement remade by hand at every site was shortened to its first term at all four**. Renamed to the concept the metric itself carries - **Built-up oversized blocks** - across the cover readout in build_drawings, the English key in i18n_en, and both editions of the body table, with the body now stating the full test: oversized cells that are majority built (park, campus, water and heritage each under 50 percent). The Chinese cover is byte-neutral and the English cover saves bytes. **The old label is left standing in the errata register** - history is not normalised, and the register has to still read as the defect it records. After this fix: both covers and both body editions name this number with one concept, and no exclusion is left unstated in the prose.
